newsitem.title: UK: UK Pizza Hut ad to star hapless soccer trio.
newsitem.headline: UK Pizza Hut ad to star hapless soccer trio.

text.p: Three English footballers who could have kicked themselves for missing key penalties may get the last laugh when they star in a television commercial for Pizza Hut.

Stuart Pearce, Gareth Southgate and Chris Waddle -- who have all missed vital penalities in matches against Germany -- will appear together in a commercial for the restaurant chain, a Pizza Hut spokeswoman said on Thursday.

"It's going to be humourous," the spokeswoman told Reuters. She declined to provide further details, but said it will be in the same vein as the Pizza Hut advert that stars Damon Hill, the top British Grand Prix driver, and television sports commentator Murray Walker.
The Pizza Hut spokeswoman declined to disclose how much Pearce, Southgage and Waddle are being paid.
Hill and Walker were reportedly paid 100,000 pounds each for their ad in which Walker insists on providing a running commentary of the pizza meal that he and Hill share.

The commercial featuring the hapless soccer trio, which is to be filmed soon, will run indefinitely beginning in early November. It will appear on commercial television throughout the UK, with most of the ads running on terrestrial television, the Pizza Hut spokeswoman said.
Pearce and Waddle each missed penalties in the 1990 World Cup semi-final against Germany. Southgate missed the penalty that would have brought England to the Euro '96 final last June.
Pizza Hut in the UK is jointly owned by U.S.-based PepsiCo , developer of the pizza chain, and Whitbread, the British brewing and leisure group.
